title: How to Prepare for Knee Replacement Surgery: A Simple Checklist
metaDescription: Preparing for knee replacement: medical checks, medicines, dental work, exercises beforehand and getting your home ready. Easy checklist.
intro: Good preparation makes knee replacement safer and recovery easier. Start several weeks ahead with a medical check, sort out your medicines, finish any dental work, strengthen your legs, and get your home ready. Follow the instructions your own surgical team gives you, as hospitals vary.

sections.heading: What should I do several weeks before surgery?
sections.body: Have a general health check with your doctor. OrthoInfo says blood tests, an ECG, a chest X-ray and a urine test may be done. If you have diabetes, high blood pressure or heart problems, get them reviewed early so any changes are made before the date.

sections.heading: What do I do about my medicines?
sections.body: Give your team a list of everything you take, including vitamins and over-the-counter medicines. Some may need to be stopped a week or two before surgery, and blood thinners, insulin and steroids need a plan. Never stop a prescribed medicine on your own.

sections.heading: Do dental work, smoking and alcohol matter?
sections.body: Yes. Finish dental treatment well before surgery and avoid dental work for several weeks after, because of infection risk. Cut down or stop smoking, which slows healing. OrthoInfo advises no alcohol for at least 48 hours before surgery.

sections.heading: Should I do exercises before surgery?
sections.body: Yes, if you can. A review of trials found that exercises before knee replacement improve leg strength and function before surgery, with some extra benefit in the first weeks afterwards. Strong thigh muscles help recovery. A physiotherapist can show you suitable exercises and teach you the after-surgery exercises.

sections.heading: How do I get my home ready?
sections.body: Plan for walking aids at first. OrthoInfo suggests removing loose rugs, keeping things at arm level, preparing meals ahead, and arranging help for the first days. A shower chair, grab bar and raised toilet seat help. Ask us how to manage an Indian-style toilet and floor seating in the early weeks.

sections.heading: What about the day before and the day of surgery?
sections.body: Follow your hospital's instructions on fasting and washing. Pack your bag, bring your medicine list and reports, and make sure a family member can stay with you. Write down your questions for the surgeon beforehand.

faqs.q: How early should I start preparing?
Can I eat before knee replacement surgery?
faqs.a: You will be told when to stop eating and drinking; follow your hospital's instructions.

faqs.q: Do I need to lose weight before surgery?
faqs.a: A healthier weight helps, but we talk about it kindly and individually.
Dental problems should be treated before surgery because of infection risk.

faqs.q: What should I bring to hospital?
faqs.a: Medicine list, reports, comfortable clothes, walking aids if advised, and a helper.

faqs.q: How long will I stay in hospital?
faqs.a: Most people go home 1 to 4 days after surgery, according to the NHS.
